stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML topics including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
The mention of 'safetensors' indicates relevance to modern, efficient model deployment.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: An Israeli firm is sending spyware through online ads, researchers say
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: An Israeli ad tech firm was found to be facilitating spyware distribution via online advertisements.
The attack vector allows for zero-click infections, meaning devices can be compromised simply by viewing an ad.
The investigation, conducted by Citizen Lab and Confiant, implicated high-profile targets, including Al Jazeera.

stories.title: Researchers use AI to design proteins that cut up other proteins
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: AI is being utilized to engineer novel proteins.
These designed proteins possess the capability to break down highly stable molecular bonds.
This represents a significant advancement in protein design and potentially has broad implications for biochemistry and medicine.

stories.title: Recording device hidden in toilet paper found in top-secret OpenAI meeting room
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: An OpenAI engineer was caught with a recording device hidden in a toilet paper roll within a top-secret meeting room.
The FBI has charged the engineer with espionage, suggesting foreign spy involvement.
The individual faces severe penalties, including up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

stories.title: Zero-Click Spyware Delivered via Targeted Ads: AdFection
stories.author: jcomp
bullet_points: AdFection is a zero-click spyware threat.
It is delivered through targeted advertisements.
This represents a significant and dangerous evolution in digital attack vectors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The tags confirm its association with major AI frameworks like transformers and the Llama family.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed to run locally, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured $88 million in funding.
The funding round involved prominent investors including Benchmark, Y Combinator, and 8VC.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses.
The updated engine also delivers faster response times and lower memory usage.

stories.title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
stories.author: Cees G. M. Snoek
bullet_points: Addresses the rigidity of fixed-size transformer models (S, B, L) when facing heterogeneous hardware and fluctuating workloads.
Proposes a novel, retraining-free method to 'elastify' pre-trained transformers.
Enables a single model to dynamically adapt across a continuum of computational budgets on-the-fly.

stories.title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
stories.author: Cees G. M. Snoek
bullet_points: Addresses the rigidity of current transformer models, which are limited to fixed sizes (S, B, L).
Proposes a novel, retraining-free method to make pre-trained transformers 'elastic'.
Enables a single model to adapt dynamically across a continuum of computational budgets and workloads.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the deployment of AI agents using its cloud models.
The integration allows these AI agents to run securely within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for safe and scalable deployment of AI agents.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama now integrates support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution for making typed decisions.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-source LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models and hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Shelly’s new presence sensor simultaneously detects up to 10 people without a camera
stories.author: Andrew Liszewski
bullet_points: Shelly has released a new Presence Gen4 sensor for smart home automation.
The sensor uses mmWave radar technology to detect up to 10 people without using a camera.
This offers a privacy-focused alternative to traditional camera-based presence detection.

stories.title: Microsoft’s new Photos app combines your PC, OneDrive, and iCloud galleries
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Microsoft has significantly redesigned the Windows 11 Photos app.
The new app integrates photo and video galleries from local PC storage, OneDrive, and iCloud.
The goal is to streamline photo management by providing a unified viewing experience across platforms.

stories.title: How Windows is being optimized for Nvidia’s RTX Spark laptops
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft and Nvidia are collaborating on the next generation of AI PCs, specifically featuring RTX Spark laptops.
The launch event highlighted the increasing focus on AI capabilities within consumer hardware.
The partnership signals a major push by both companies to integrate advanced AI processing into mainstream Windows devices.

stories.title: Nobody is safe from celebrity AI deepfakes
stories.author: Mia Sato
bullet_points: The article discusses the danger of celebrity AI deepfakes.
A specific example involves a deepfake image of actress Mia Goth.
The piece highlights the potential for malicious use of AI in social media contexts.

stories.title: Fridge hack costing millions and sparking fires stemmed from poor security
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A security vulnerability in outdated devices led to a major incident affecting 700 supermarkets.
The 'fridge hack' exploited poor security practices, allowing unauthorized access to connected appliances.
The breach resulted in significant financial costs and safety hazards, including fires.

stories.title: NATO may redeploy anti-drone defenses as attacks sink more Black Sea shipping
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: NATO is reportedly considering redeploying anti-drone defenses.
The impetus for this shift is increased maritime incidents in the Black Sea.
Suspected Russian drones have caused damage or sunk five ships near Bulgaria and Romania.

stories.title: Things are finally looking up for NASA's first missions to Venus in a generation
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: NASA is making progress on its planned missions to Venus.
The positive outlook is prompting NASA to increase staffing and accelerate development.
This represents a significant step forward for Venus exploration after a long hiatus.

stories.title: Schools across US protest FCC plan that could disconnect kids from Internet
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: The FCC is facing protests from schools regarding a plan that could impact student internet access.
The FCC chair has threatened the E-Rate fund, a program supporting school connectivity.
The FCC's stance reportedly blames schools for issues related to students' screen time.

stories.title: Modeling and Understanding Neural Weights of Humanoid Policies with Diffusion
stories.author: Koushil Sreenath
bullet_points: The research focuses on humanoid control policies, a rapidly advancing area in robotics.
It addresses a gap by investigating the direct modeling and generation of neural network weights, rather than just training them conventionally.
The study utilizes Diffusion models to explore the distribution of high-performing humanoid control network weights.

stories.title: Hierarchical Residual Policy Learning for Real-World Mobile Manipulation with Sparse Human Guidance
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of real-world fine-tuning in Mobile Manipulation (MoMa) due to high-dimensional action spaces.
Introduces HiRe-MoMa, a framework utilizing a Hierarchical Residual Architecture for stable and sample-efficient fine-tuning.
Focuses on improving complex MoMa systems using sparse human guidance.

stories.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
stories.author: Jiaxuan You
bullet_points: The research addresses the computational bottleneck in training language agents caused by expensive long-horizon rollouts.
It critiques existing methods in agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) that fail to effectively utilize intermediate-step supervision.
The proposed method involves 'Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting' to better leverage step-wise information beyond just the final scalar reward.

stories.title: Continuum Attention
stories.author: Afshin Khadangi
bullet_points: Introduces Continuum Attention (CA), a novel causal Transformer attention operator.
Replaces discrete key/value lookup with integration over a continuous, piecewise linear memory curve.
Enables exact normalized attention calculation from closed-form exponential moments, simplifying gradient computation.

stories.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
stories.author: Hwee Tou Ng
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of training AI agents to master complex, visually rich video games.
Current methods are limited by reliance on large demonstrations and difficulty in creating scalable training environments.
The paper introduces 'Player-1' to improve game-agent learning by leveraging synthetic experience.

stories.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
stories.author: Peng Qi
bullet_points: LLM agents exhibit interface dependence, meaning their performance degrades when the input interface is slightly altered from the training setup.
The paper proposes 'Cross-Interface Consistency Training' to improve LLM agent robustness against interface variations.
This method aims to decouple the agent's core competence from the specific interface it was trained on, enhancing out-of-distribution performance.

stories.title: Beyond LLM Judge: Mechanical Verification for Agentic Autoformalization
stories.author: Michael R. Douglas
bullet_points: Introduces a new verification method for Lean formalizations that moves beyond relying solely on LLM judgments.
Combines LLM-based semantic review with rigorous mechanical numerical and vacuity checks to improve error detection.
Applies this method within an Extract-Verify-Proof pipeline to construct the Formalized Library of Mathematical Functions (FLMF).

stories.title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Taylor W. Killian
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in On-Policy Distillation (OPD) where the teacher fails to provide reliable supervision on incorrect student rollouts.
The core problem identified is the 'recoverability of the teacher,' which breaks down when the student makes errors.
The proposed solution, CriticOPD, uses a critic mechanism to allow the teacher to critique incorrect rollouts, thereby restoring reliable supervision.

stories.title: Modeling and Understanding Neural Weights of Humanoid Policies with Diffusion
stories.author: Koushil Sreenath
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in humanoid control by focusing on modeling the distribution of learned neural network weights, rather than just training the networks conventionally.
The study investigates the feasibility of generating high-performing humanoid control networks directly within the weight space using diffusion models.
This work contributes to the field of robot learning by offering a new perspective on understanding and manipulating the internal representations (weights) of complex control policies.

stories.title: Hierarchical Residual Policy Learning for Real-World Mobile Manipulation with Sparse Human Guidance
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces HiRe-MoMa, a new framework for Mobile Manipulation (MoMa) fine-tuning.
Addresses real-world challenges in MoMa, such as high-dimensional action spaces and module coupling.
Utilizes a Hierarchical Residual Architecture to achieve stable and sample-efficient fine-tuning with sparse human guidance.

stories.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
stories.author: Jiaxuan You
bullet_points: The research addresses the high computational cost of long-horizon rollouts in training language agents.
It critiques existing methods in agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) that fail to utilize intermediate-step supervision effectively.
The proposed method involves 'Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting' to overcome the limitations of standard scalar reward signals for intermediate steps.

stories.title: Continuum Attention
stories.author: Afshin Khadangi
bullet_points: Introduces Continuum Attention (CA), a novel causal Transformer attention operator.
Replaces discrete key/value lookup with integration over a continuous, piecewise linear memory curve.
Achieves exact normalized attention via closed-form exponential moments, simplifying gradient calculations.

stories.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
stories.author: Xu Han
bullet_points: Addresses the memory and computational cost associated with large Key-Value (KV) caches in long-context LLMs.
Proposes 'Latent Compaction,' a method that learns a compact, document-specific cache via test-time training.
Uses initialization techniques based on reconstruction importance, teacher attention, and key-space diversity to maintain information integrity.

stories.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
stories.author: Peng Qi
bullet_points: LLM agents exhibit interface dependence, meaning their performance degrades when the input interface is slightly altered from the training environment.
The research proposes 'Cross-Interface Consistency Training' to mitigate this interface binding and improve LLM agent robustness.
The core problem addressed is that current methods only broaden dependence across a distribution of training interfaces, failing against out-of-distribution perturbations.

stories.title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Taylor W. Killian
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in On-Policy Distillation (OPD), where the teacher model fails to provide reliable supervision on incorrect student rollouts.
It introduces CriticOPD, a new method that utilizes a critic to allow the teacher to critique and correct incorrect student outputs.
The research focuses on improving the robustness and reliability of knowledge transfer between teacher and student models in sequence generation tasks.

stories.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
stories.author: Xu Han
bullet_points: Addresses the memory and computational bottleneck caused by large Key-Value (KV) caches in long-context LLMs.
Introduces 'Latent Compaction,' a method that learns a compact, document-specific cache via test-time training.
Uses initialization strategies based on reconstruction importance, teacher attention, and key-space diversity to maintain information fidelity.

stories.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
stories.author: Peng Qi
bullet_points: LLM agents exhibit poor robustness because their competence becomes tied to the specific interface they were trained on.
Interface perturbations (like renaming actions) that don't change the underlying task degrade agent performance.
The paper proposes 'Cross-Interface Consistency Training' to improve LLM agent robustness against out-of-distribution interface changes.

stories.title: Manacá-1B-Instruct-2: Reproducible Safety Alignment for a Native Brazilian-Portuguese LLM. Negative DPO Results, a Controlled Composition Scan, and a Silent Failure Mode of the LLM Judge
stories.author: Fabio André Machado Porto
bullet_points: Introduces Manacá-1B-Instruct-2, a second-generation safety-aligned LLM specifically for Brazilian Portuguese (PT-BR).
Addresses a gap in the field by documenting negative results from DPO alignment attempts, offering transparency.
Highlights technical findings, including a controlled composition scan and the identification of a 'silent failure mode' in the LLM judge.

stories.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
stories.author: Matei Zaharia
bullet_points: LLM agents are demonstrating capability in automated research and idea discovery through iterative refinement.
Scaling automated research via longer iteration, parallel agents, or agent communication eventually leads to performance plateaus.
The paper suggests that 'forgetting' is a necessary mechanism to overcome the limitations of accumulating extensive history in LLM agents.

stories.title: PerSo: Investigating Facets of LLMs' Social Intelligence in Real-World Persuasion Scenarios
stories.author: Yadollah Yaghoobzadeh
bullet_points: The research investigates the 'social intelligence' of Large Language Models (LLMs) using real-world persuasion scenarios.
Social intelligence is broken down into two components: cognitive intelligence (inferring mental states) and behavioral intelligence (selecting appropriate social actions).
Persuasion serves as a natural and complex testbed to evaluate both the cognitive and behavioral aspects of LLM social capabilities.

stories.title: PrismaCoder: Pushing the Boundaries of Open Multimodal Code Intelligence through Decomposed Rubric Synthesis
stories.author: Jiahui Gao
bullet_points: PrismaCoder addresses the need for open multimodal code intelligence, bridging symbolic code with visual execution outputs.
The research highlights the growing demand for AI models to generate complex visual artifacts (charts, webpages) from text or images.
The work aims to democratize progress in this area, contrasting with proprietary models that currently lead but keep their training data closed.

stories.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
stories.author: Chuan-Wei Kuo
bullet_points: ReaDy introduces a new speculative decoding method designed to improve LLM generation efficiency.
It leverages Hybrid Linear Attention (HLA) models, which maintain compact recurrent states for contextual awareness.
The method addresses limitations in feature-based drafters by using HLA states as a dynamic context source for drafting.

stories.title: Lost in Translation: Why Lower Bias Scores Don't Mean Fairer Models
stories.author: Harsh Kumar
bullet_points: The study challenges the standard practice of using simple average stereotype score differences between English and other languages as a measure of fairness in multilingual models.
Researchers investigate how much of the observed 'difference' in bias scores is merely statistical noise, rather than genuine model bias.
The methodology involves rigorous testing by rephrasing English test items and injecting deliberate shifts to validate the sensitivity of the bias audits across eight languages.

stories.title: AdaRSI: On-Demand Recursive Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
stories.author: Daling Wang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: failure during long-horizon, unseen tasks.
Proposes 'AdaRSI,' a novel framework for Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) in embodied agents.
Distinguishes between failures in how an executor is called versus inherent limitations in its capabilities, guiding when to update model weights.

stories.title: Prompt injection in HTTP headers: what 217M web responses show
stories.author: panoramas4good
bullet_points: The story investigates prompt injection vulnerabilities specifically within HTTP headers.
Analysis is based on a large dataset of 217 million web responses.
This highlights a growing security risk in how web applications handle input beyond the body.
